elements.evidence: Rendered 12.4 now reads: "Customer is subject to no restriction on soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee." The former one-sided bar ("shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward") is gone, and no other provision in the cited text imposes a solicitation restraint on Customer; 12.3 reinforces this by recording that Customer has made no no-hire commitment.

The proposal eliminates the restriction entirely rather than converting it into a two-way covenant; no operative language binds either Party, so there is no mutual restriction. (This is by design: the drafter targeted the preferred level.)

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — no restriction survives in 12.4, so no personnel of any category are covered; the scope limit is satisfied vacuously.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — the term-plus-24-month period was deleted and no replacement duration exists, so no period exceeds 12 months.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — with no restriction in 12.4, general advertising is unrestricted; 12.3 separately confirms Customer may hire "any person who responds to general recruitment."

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — the "regardless of how the employee applies" language that captured unsolicited approaches is deleted and no restriction remains to apply to them.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The express no-hire words "hire, or employ" are removed; rendered 12.4 affirmatively states Customer is subject to no restriction on hiring or employing Vendor employees.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the sole non-solicit (Section 12.4) is replaced with an express confirmation that Customer bears no solicitation, hiring or employment restriction, which is exactly the single preferred element.

Fallback is not satisfied (no mutual covenant exists), but that is irrelevant because the preferred checklist is fully met; the comment appropriately offers the mutual 12-month, involvement-limited, carve-out-bearing structure as a fallback rather than drafting it.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to the one sentence of 12.4, adds no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or extraneous requirement, and leaves 12.3 and the rest of Article 12 untouched. The affirmative restatement (rather than pure deletion) is a concise, non-expansive way to record the preferred outcome and does not create an operative duplicate of 12.3, which speaks only to Customer's absence of a no-hire commitment and to general-recruitment hiring.

Intent preserved: no defined term, cross-reference or numbering is disturbed, no retained sentence contradicts the new 12.4, and the prior internal conflict between the old 12.4 no-hire and 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no no-hire commitment is resolved rather than aggravated.

Drafting note (non-blocking): the rationale mistakenly refers to "[t]he separate Section 12.4 non-compete" — that cross-reference should read 12.3 (or be deleted) so the internal note matches the operative text.

Severity elevated because the original clause sat in walk-away territory — an express no-hire covering all Vendor employees for the term plus twenty-four months, with unsolicited applicants expressly captured.
